Response: John, Kate, Jack, Luke—before we choose, I propose we each catch 12 tons this month instead of 10. That gives each of us $12,000 rather than $10,000: an extra $2,000 apiece, or $10,000 across the group.

If everyone sticks to 12, we catch 60 tons and leave 40. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability or 80 tons with 25% probability. By contrast, five catches of 10 leave 50, which returns to 100 under either recovery outcome. So the extra income comes with a real tradeoff: a one-in-four chance of starting next month 20 tons below full capacity. I’m not claiming 12 is the best long-run policy or that replenishment is guaranteed.

My proposal is a one-month agreement, followed by reassessment using the actual stock. Leaving 40 avoids the collapse threshold if everyone follows through, but our choices are private and simultaneous, and future agreements aren’t enforceable. That makes explicit commitments important, though they aren’t guarantees.

I’ll commit to catching 12 tons this month. Luke, will you join me in supporting this proposal? John, Kate, and Jack, will each of you explicitly commit to 12 as well? If you prefer 10 because of the recovery risk, please say so—we can discuss a lower whole-ton cap or a different allocation rather than assume anyone’s consent.
Conversation conclusion by me: no
Next speaker: Luke
